html:
The Tahue were a farming people of the coastal plain of central Sinaloa in north-western Mexico, around the valley of Culiacán. Their language is thought to have been Uto-Aztecan, but little of it was recorded.

They lived in large villages along the rivers, irrigating maize, beans and cotton, heirs of the Aztatlán culture that had linked this coast to central Mexico. In 1531 the conquistador Nuño de Guzmán invaded their country with great brutality and founded San Miguel de Culiacán, for years the northernmost Spanish town of New Spain. Disease, slave raids and forced labour destroyed the Tahue within a few generations. To the north lived the Mayo.
